metadata.title: OpenBMT capability review
metadata.scope_note: Research only. Four bounded first-party product corpora, separate card components, and Bitcoin-native requirements. No whole-product exhaustiveness, tested compatibility, feature parity, product approval or release readiness is claimed.
metadata.default_rule: Match or improve every retained merchant job and documented variant unless an explicit mechanism exception or scope deferral is approved. A deferral remains an open requirement.
metadata.normalization_policy: Only coordinator-approved narrow aliases are combined. Related families aid navigation and never erase variant requirements.
metadata.status_policy: Related evidence is not parity. No mapping means not assessed, never absent. Engine primitives, sandbox flows and scoped tests do not establish a complete merchant workflow.
metadata.source_count_note: Source records are exact page/section inspections; repeated URLs across sections or researchers count separately. Coverage rows are topics, not an equal-weight percentage of a product.
metadata.workflow: Research/planning complete as a bounded snapshot; unresolved branches and production hypotheses remain explicit gates. No application implementation in this phase.

capabilities.capability: Docker backup script archives database dumps, generated secrets and Docker volumes, with optional archive encryption, and restarts the BTCPay stack afterward.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Operator can create a restorable instance data archive while excluding re-downloadable blockchain data and caches.
unmet_scope: BTO-C017: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C017: Provide a guided backup job with off-host copy, retention, and restore-test status.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C017: Merchant can retain its own payment records and wallet metadata without relying on a payment processor's custodial database.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C017: Backup downtime, encryption passphrase custody and operator responsibility add burden; archive does not preserve blockchain data or prove funds can be recovered.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C017: Restore a recent encrypted and unencrypted sample into isolated compatible deployment and compare stores, records, wallet metadata and service readiness.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Docker recovery requires both saved data archives and a prepared compatible deployment profile; generated Compose file is disposable, while volumes, databases and generated secrets are persistent state.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Operator can prepare a destination using deployment settings and restore persistent state without assuming generated configuration alone is a complete backup.
unmet_scope: BTO-C039: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C039: Generate an exportable deployment manifest alongside backup and run destination compatibility preflight.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C039: Merchant can reconstruct its own processor and node deployment from retained state rather than depend on a platform-hosted processor.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C039: Self-hosting means merchant must preserve configuration, secrets and version compatibility; large blockchain must resync and delays readiness.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C039: Backup plus retained manifest rebuilds compatible isolated deployment, restores data and verifies chain sync without manual reconstruction of undocumented parameters.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Operator must separately arrange protected off-host storage and retention; default backup script replaces the local archive and does not provide retention or remote copy.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: A merchant can avoid treating one local archive as a resilient backup by creating a separate copy/retention process.
unmet_scope: BTO-C018: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C018: Include optional built-in encrypted offsite copies, rotation policy, and restore drill reminders.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C018: A recoverable local node/store operation supports merchant independence from third-party processors.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C018: Offsite encryption expands key custody obligations and recurring storage cost; backups must be tested rather than assumed.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C018: A scheduled backup creates versioned protected remote copies, reports failures, and a selected retained copy restores in isolation.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Restore validates archive mode and Bitcoin LND destination conditions, restores volumes/database/secrets and has safeguards against overlaying existing LND data.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Operator can restore instance data while reducing the risk of mixing restored wallet/channel state with unrelated destination data.
unmet_scope: BTO-C019: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C019: Turn restore into a preflight/recovery checklist showing archive mode, config compatibility, LND data presence and post-restore verification steps.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C019: Recovery of a self-run payment stack can preserve merchant operational data and on-chain wallet monitoring under merchant control.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C019: Incorrect stale channel state can risk funds; restore requires operator skill and does not validate external network readiness.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C019: Restore refuses wrong-mode or nonempty-LND overlays, then isolated recovery verifies store data and on-chain sync without connecting stale Lightning state to peers.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: A Docker operator can create a migration-mode backup that includes Bitcoin LND channel graph data, leaves source stack stopped and restores to a compatible prepared destination in stopped state.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: A merchant can move a healthy LND node while preserving current open-channel database state if source remains stopped and migration snapshot is current.
unmet_scope: BTO-C021: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C021: Offer a guarded migration workflow with source freeze verification and destination readiness comparison.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C021: Allows a merchant to operate and migrate its self-custodial Lightning node rather than moving funds into a hosted custodian.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C021: Migration has a strict single-active-node invariant and requires correct channel state, compatible deployment and sufficient operator expertise.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C021: Migration drill confirms source stopped and unchanged, destination restored stopped, channel state matches, and exactly one node is started.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Recover on-chain receipt and authority after device loss
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Merchant can restore keys or independently recover funds and still reconcile all issued/late addresses.
unmet_scope: BTC-C013: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTC-C013: Provide a recovery checklist and independently verifiable backup freshness/coverage indicator.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTC-C013: Independent key recovery can avoid a vendor account being necessary to regain authority; prove offline restore.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTC-C013: Merchant bears backup secrecy, physical security, and operational testing; backup exposure increases theft risk.
acceptance_tests: BTC-C013: Conduct clean-device recovery using merchant-held artifacts; verify spend authority and identify every issued address mapped to open/late sales.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: BTCPay's Docker backup guide says Core Lightning's existing backup behavior is unchanged and its LND SCB recovery procedure does not apply to CLN; the inspected official pages do not specify an equivalent end-to-end CLN or Eclair restore procedure.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Operator must use implementation-specific channel recovery guidance and cannot assume LND seed/SCB steps recover another implementation.
unmet_scope: BTO-C040: Box/wallet backup is not BTCPay Docker archive restore, standalone checkout ledger recovery, or Lightning channel recovery.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C040: Publish and link a BTCPay per-implementation backup/restore decision tree with tested, version-qualified steps.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C040: Self-hosted LN implementation choice supports merchant autonomy but recovery documentation fragmentation increases risk across node implementations.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C040: A common BTCPay archive can simplify some data recovery, yet implementation-specific channel-state rules cannot be flattened safely into one generic restore recipe.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C040: For every supported LN implementation, isolated backup and restore drills establish state preservation or documented recovery path without starting stale channel state against peers.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Preserve channel state safely across backup and restore
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Merchant does not mistake a key backup for a complete live Lightning node recovery.
unmet_scope: BTC-C019: No parity or support claim is made; inspect the exact workflow and code path before treating this as absent or supported.
improvement_hypotheses: BTC-C019: Expose backup health and recovery mode separately from key custody; gate Lightning offers on validated freshness and integrity.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTC-C019: Merchant-owned keys support independent control but do not make Lightning channel state independent of peers or persistence.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTC-C019: Channel state requires careful consistency; recovery can require peers, force close, on-chain fees, and delayed access.
acceptance_tests: BTC-C019: Inject stale/missing manager and monitor backups; verify Lightning stays disabled until safe recovery, then reconcile balances and close outcomes.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Operator should record implementation-specific Lightning node recovery material before transacting; guide directs LND users to seed backup and CLN users to hsm_secret backup.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Merchant can preserve required node recovery material separately from ordinary store/on-chain wallet backups.
unmet_scope: BTO-C026: No positive support/parity claim is made. The referenced evidence does not implement the claim’s central action or its required UI/operational boundary.
improvement_hypotheses: BTO-C026: Create implementation-aware setup checks that verify protected copies of all required recovery items without uploading secrets.
bitcoin_hypotheses: BTO-C026: Self-custody is preserved only if merchant can recover the LN node; documented backup discipline enables that goal.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: BTO-C026: Additional sensitive material increases secure-storage burden and wrong/stale backups do not guarantee funds recovery.
acceptance_tests: BTO-C026: For each supported implementation, operator completes an isolated documented recovery drill with correct current material and no secret uploaded to BTCPay service.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Toast guide review documents connection restoration and offline synchronization, but does not establish backup/restore or disaster recovery guarantees.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Recover menu, order and configuration data after hardware loss, corruption or prolonged outage.
unmet_scope: TOO-C039: No parity or support claim is made; inspect the exact workflow and code path before treating this as absent or supported.
improvement_hypotheses: TOO-C039: Could expose tested restore points and operational recovery status; measure time to restore sales-critical operations.
bitcoin_hypotheses: TOO-C039: Recovery expectations are independent of payment custody.
bitcoin_tradeoffs: TOO-C039: Bitcoin funding cannot recover lost catalog, orders or staff configuration.
acceptance_tests: TOO-C039: Obtain applicable recovery/backup documentation and test a documented restore scenario without live merchant data loss.
capabilities.comparison_note: Every vendor variant and its qualifiers remains an obligation to assess. Group membership does not establish identical behavior, implementation, compatibility or parity.

capabilities.capability: Close Out Day provides a dynamic daily Z report and sequenced closeout actions.
capabilities.merchant_outcome: Close operational tasks and retain end-of-day sales/cash summary.

bitcoin_tradeoffs: TOO-C025: Different settlement lifecycles may require added closeout ledger and finality controls; test against existing closeout sequence.
acceptance_tests: TOO-C025: Exercise each closeout state and confirm the available actions, permissions, dynamic Z report, automated closeout hour and offline block.

vendors.scope: Public merchant/user documentation for store setup, Bitcoin receiving, invoices and checkout lifecycle, merchant-facing POS, payment requests, subscriptions, refund claims and payout review, receipts, and reporting. limitations: Evidence is public documentation only, not observed behavior on a live BTCPay instance; documentation is not compatibility testing.

Public guide pages were inspected for assigned merchant branches, not every linked page or every branch in the BTCPay documentation corpus; coverage explicitly records exclusions and unresolved areas.

The user-facing docs make feature availability dependent on instance administrator, enabled apps/plugins, permissions, wallet configuration, SMTP, version and device. No specific hosting plan or edition was assumed.

POS tips/custom amount behavior, form validation/retention, receipt layout and hardware matrix, offline acceptance, staff/multilocation/inventory/tax closeout, and some failure recovery details remain unknown where the inspected docs do not specify them.

Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning are different payment rails. This bundle treats on-chain Bitcoin as the primary scope, notes Lightning only where invoice settlement documentation requires it, and does not merge optional altcoin plugins or third-party Lightning services into core Bitcoin capability claims.

No claim establishes that any feature is absent when documentation is incomplete. Improvement hypotheses and acceptance tests are proposals for OpenBMT evaluation, not statements that an incumbent feature has been tested or that OpenBMT currently implements it.

Target instance version, plugins, hosting, deployment profile, authentication policies, wallet type, and Lightning implementation can change behavior. Use that instance's /docs and current operator configuration for implementation decisions.

claims.capability: A merchant can create a store with a business/project name and default invoice currency.
claims.merchant_outcome: Establishes the store context used for payment and checkout settings.
claims.trigger: After registration or from the store selector
claims.behavior: The user names the store, chooses a default currency and creates it; store settings can later be changed.
preconditions: Access to an instance permitting account registration and store creation
qualifiers: Registration and available options are administrator-controlled.
recovery_edge_cases: If registration is unavailable, the merchant must obtain access from the instance administrator; no self-service bypass is documented.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Test a guided setup that previews which choices affect invoice display and allows a merchant to verify currency and price source before first sale.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin-only receiving can reduce checkout-method configuration complexity; test whether a first-time merchant can connect the intended wallet and create a verified test invoice without needing a hosted processor account.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Direct wallet control shifts setup and recovery responsibility to the merchant; the setup should make wallet mode and seed custody consequences clear without asking users to expose a seed.
claims.acceptance_test: On a fresh permitted account, a merchant creates a named store in a chosen currency, then can identify the selected store and change its default settings within 3 minutes; verify no payment is accepted until a receiving method is configured.

openbmt_mapping.mapping_rationale: The cited evidence is only a boundary or adjacent primitive; its central merchant action is not implemented in the mapped OpenBMT workflow. This remains unassessed rather than a finding of absence.
openbmt_mapping.unmet_scope: No positive support/parity claim is made. The referenced evidence does not implement the claim’s central action or its required UI/operational boundary.

claims.capability: A merchant can connect an existing public wallet, create a watch-only wallet, or create a hot wallet for on-chain receiving.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allows selection of a receiving setup with different signing and custody arrangements.
claims.trigger: Wallet setup in the selected store
claims.behavior: Existing wallet public data can be imported, a new watch-only wallet can retain public receiving data while private key is erased from server, or a hot wallet can keep a spend key on the server.
preconditions: Bitcoin wallet feature enabled by server administrator
qualifiers: The hot wallet convenience/security tradeoff is explicit; wallet setup option availability is admin controlled.
recovery_edge_cases: A watch-only wallet needs a recovery seed or external signer to spend; a lost seed for a generated wallet may prevent recovery. Documentation advises testing recovery/signing before significant value.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Measure whether a guided wallet choice explains receive versus spend capability and signing responsibility before setup, then verify with a successful test receipt and restore drill.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin allows the merchant to receive to a wallet they control; evaluate whether standard public-key import and external signing can make that control understandable and safe for a nontechnical merchant.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Self-custody removes intermediary control but makes key backup and signer recovery the merchant's responsibility; hot-wallet compromise can expose funds.
claims.acceptance_test: For each supported wallet mode, create a receive invoice and verify the address against the intended wallet; attempt recovery/signing with documented credentials before accepting production funds; never enter an existing seed into the server.

claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin invoice checkout can direct payment to the merchant's configured wallet; test whether the merchant can confirm wallet receipt and invoice linkage without reconciling a separate processor balance.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: The rate lock and expiry introduce time pressure, while on-chain confirmation policy can delay fulfillment; communicate those costs and let merchant fulfillment policy govern release.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a small invoice with an order reference, open checkout in a separate browser, pay from a separate Bitcoin wallet, and confirm the invoice displays the correct payment and settlement state.

claims.capability: An invoice exposes payment and settlement state so the merchant can distinguish new, processing, settled, expired, and invalid payments.
claims.merchant_outcome: Supports fulfillment decisions based on actual payment progress and configured confirmation policy.
claims.trigger: Customer pays a Bitcoin invoice
claims.behavior: On-chain full payment can remain processing until configured confirmation conditions are met; Lightning payment normally settles without on-chain confirmations. The merchant can inspect invoice status and payment details.
preconditions: Invoice created and store payment method configured
qualifiers: Confirmation count and monitoring policy are store/wallet settings; Lightning operations are out of scope here.
recovery_edge_cases: Do not fulfill merely on broadcast; inspect status. A fully paid transaction that fails settlement monitoring may become invalid and needs business review.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Test whether the status page explains the next merchant action and expected confirmation condition for each state, reducing premature fulfillment and unnecessary refreshes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin settlement evidence can be checked against the public transaction and confirmation count; test a merchant-readable status that links transaction evidence to the configured fulfillment threshold.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: On-chain finality is not immediate and a zero-confirmation acceptance policy adds risk; the merchant must choose a policy appropriate to goods value and loss tolerance.
claims.acceptance_test: For an on-chain invoice, observe new, processing, then settled as confirmations accrue under the configured threshold; verify a staff member does not mark the order fulfilled before the chosen threshold. Record Lightning as a distinct, separately verified payment-method case.

openbmt_mapping.mapping_rationale: Related Regtest observation states are recorded under the OpenBMT payment-evidence capability. The complete documented invoice base-state workflow is not demonstrated.
openbmt_mapping.unmet_scope: Regtest prototype only; no production confirmation policy or automated fulfillment decision.

claims.capability: Invoice details and filters expose partial, overpaid, late, invalid, and manually marked exceptions for merchant review.
claims.merchant_outcome: Helps identify payment discrepancies that need a fulfillment, additional-payment, or refund decision.
claims.trigger: Payment amount or timing differs from invoice expectation, settlement fails, or staff manually changes status
claims.behavior: Base invoice status is accompanied by an exception indicator; the merchant can search/filter unusual invoices and inspect amount, payment method, transaction and status history before action.
preconditions: Invoice has received relevant payment activity or manual status change
qualifiers: Manual marking is an accounting decision and does not establish on-chain confirmation.
recovery_edge_cases: Partial payments can result from a wrong amount or payment-service fee; late or partial payments on expired invoices require review, and archived invoices continue to be monitored.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Measure resolution time and mis-fulfillment rate with a guided exception queue that presents amount short/over, timing, transaction evidence, and permitted next actions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin's transaction-level payment evidence may support clear short/over reconciliation; test whether the merchant can map each transaction to invoice amount without assuming a third party will net or correct it.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Fee deduction and exchange-wallet behavior can leave an invoice short; accepting a tolerance trades revenue certainty for fewer manual exceptions, and manual settlement marking carries fulfillment risk.
claims.acceptance_test: Exercise underpayment, overpayment, payment after expiry, unconfirmed/invalid payment, and manual mark. For each, confirm invoice remains findable in the unusual filter, displayed exception matches scenario, and fulfillment remains blocked pending an explicit merchant decision.

openbmt_mapping.mapping_rationale: Related partial/late/excess payment evidence does not demonstrate the documented invoice details, filters and manual exception-state actions.

claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Public transaction identifiers can reveal sensitive purchase/payment patterns if shared broadly; restrict staff access and minimize customer data in search results.

claims.capability: A merchant can define an offering and plans, then share a plan checkout for customers to subscribe or add credit.
claims.merchant_outcome: Supports recurring service or donation enrollment with tier and billing-period choices.
claims.actor: Merchant defines offering/plan; customer selects plan and pays
claims.trigger: Merchant creates offering and shares plan checkout link
claims.behavior: Plans define price and period; checkout can create a subscriber, collect an email and begin a paid or trial enrollment. Bitcoin subscription semantics are manual period payments or pre-funded credit deductions, not an automatic wallet debit.
preconditions: Subscriptions feature available on instance; store payment method and any required customer email flow configured
qualifiers: Plan and subscriber features/intervals vary by documented subscription version; service must enforce entitlements itself.
recovery_edge_cases: If balance is insufficient, customer must pay/top up or subscription may enter configured grace period then expire; optimistic activation may later be revoked if payment fails.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Test whether a customer understands renewal model, next due date, price and what access means before subscribing; show manual versus credit-based billing plainly.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin payment can fund a prepaid balance without storing a reusable debit credential; evaluate whether manual reminders or credit top-up give the merchant predictable renewal while the customer retains control over each payment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin does not provide a unified automatic recurring debit; prepaid credits require the customer to fund ahead and expose the merchant to unused-credit accounting and service-access reconciliation.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a monthly plan, complete checkout with a test subscriber, verify balance and first term, then confirm renewal only occurs with sufficient prepaid credit or a new manual payment; verify no customer wallet is charged automatically.

claims.acceptance_test: With a test subscriber, open portal through supplied link, inspect billing history, add credit and change plan where allowed; confirm another customer cannot access that subscriber by reusing a public nonsecret page URL.

claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Manual customer payment adds friction and failed email may cause unexpected lapse; optimistic activation risks access being granted before payment settles.
claims.acceptance_test: Exercise trial end, insufficient credit, grace period payment and grace expiry with test subscriber; verify access state, status history, configured email event and fallback visibility agree at each transition.

claims.acceptance_test: Issue original-rate, current-rate and payment-currency refunds with a test invoice; verify claim displays correct amount and destination entry, existing active claim cannot be duplicated, and merchant can review the claimed destination before sending.

claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: The review/signing step protects funds but adds operational work; network fees, confirmation delay and transaction irreversibility require clear expectations for customer and staff.
claims.acceptance_test: Submit two test claims, verify awaiting approval, inspect each amount/destination, cancel one, approve/sign/broadcast the other and confirm claimant sees in-progress then completed after Bitcoin confirmation.

qualifiers: POS Pro has extra sales, inventory, reports and staff features; plan/payment availability is country and subscription dependent.
recovery_edge_cases: If wrong location selected, change device location in POS settings; plan changes can be managed individually or in batches up to 250 locations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a device setup check that confirms location, country and plan before opening; measure mislocated orders and reader incompatibility.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin payment and reporting should inherit the selected merchant location; test correct stock and accounting location across stores without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Shopify's country rule described here is specifically for Shopify card readers and may not apply identically to another payment method; do not assume unsupported scope.
claims.acceptance_test: Switch POS device from one configured location to another, verify displayed location, and inspect that location's POS subscription plan in admin.

claims.capability: Review, export, and remotely close register sessions from admin
claims.merchant_outcome: Manager can reconcile sessions by location/date, retain CSV reports, and recover a session that cannot be closed on POS device.
claims.trigger: Manager reviews register reconciliation or device cannot close a session.
claims.behavior: Admin filters sessions by location and timeframe, opens session/net-payments/activity reports, exports open session activity or closed session reports, and can remotely close a session after entering cash counted and remaining drawer balance.
preconditions: User has POS channel access; session was opened in POS; report export permissions available.
qualifiers: Admin cannot open a new session; POS Pro required for cross-location cash tracking reports described separately.
recovery_edge_cases: Closing a session is irreversible; when a transaction is in progress, next completed transaction automatically opens a new session.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a remote-close confirmation with in-flight transaction and next-session impact; measure unresolved open sessions and audit corrections.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Include Bitcoin tender in payment report export with denomination and settlement state while keeping counted cash input physical; measure ledger-to-session reconciliation.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Cash session closeout does not settle Bitcoin and cannot undo a public transaction; reconcile the systems without conflating balances.
claims.acceptance_test: Filter sessions by location/date, export an open session activity report, remotely close an eligible session with counted cash, and verify the closure is logged and cannot be reopened.

claims.capability: Compare cash tracking discrepancies and payments across POS Pro locations

claims.trigger: Manager reviews cash reconciliation for one or multiple locations.
claims.behavior: Cash tracking report summarizes opening/closing discrepancies, gross/refund/net cash payments, and session list; supports location/date filters, sort and CSV export/print.
preconditions: Location is on POS Pro; staff has View payment register session history and View payment register sessions in POS channel permissions.
qualifiers: Cash-rounding regions include rounded payments in report; report shows cash/till metrics rather than general tender settlement details.
recovery_edge_cases: Mismatch definition compares previous closing count to new opening count and session expected cash to final count.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Flag repeated discrepancies across registers and annotate verified causes; measure unresolved discrepancy rate and time-to-review.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Preserve one Bitcoin payment-type line in broader payment summaries while leaving cash discrepancy computations tied only to drawer cash; verify cross-report totals.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Cash tracking is not a Bitcoin accounting report; a linked settlement report is needed to reconcile wallet receipts and merchant books.
claims.acceptance_test: With permissions at Pro location, filter by date and location, compare session discrepancy summary, export sessions, and verify totals match underlying register rows.

preconditions: Country/payment processor and compatible POS device are known; available hardware list checked.
qualifiers: Hardware-store availability varies by country; external terminal transaction is manually marked paid and POS only displays status without transaction details in described unsupported-country workflow.
recovery_edge_cases: For reliable USB hardware the POS Hub can reduce Bluetooth disconnections; model-specific troubleshooting not covered by this claim.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose region/device/processor compatibility before purchase and warn about reduced external-terminal detail; measure mis-purchases and reconciliation gaps.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant may use compatible external wallet/payment terminal alongside POS if they can reconcile status and order; validate exact supported hardware and avoid assuming native integration.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin reader or processor compatibility is documented; external terminal manual marking sacrifices detailed synchronization, and merchant must verify support without forced fiat conversion.
claims.acceptance_test: Check a selected model against official country/device table; verify reader is supported for payment provider or external terminal status/manual marking path is understood.

claims.capability: Run scheduled, staff-attributed stock count and review before quantities change
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can delegate physical counts without allowing staff to directly change inventory and approve only reviewed quantities.
claims.actor: Inventory manager and assigned POS staff
claims.trigger: Manager creates a count for a location and staff count listed products.
claims.behavior: Admin creates one-location product list; POS Pro staff scan or enter on-hand quantities, each item is attributed to staff, and staff request review; manager reviews/approves/rejects before inventory updates.
preconditions: POS Pro; count created in desktop admin and assigned to location; staff has Perform inventory counts permission; network connection.
qualifiers: Only listed items can be counted; multiple staff can count concurrently and counts combine; stale products changed during count are marked outdated.
recovery_edge_cases: Staff can continue other products and request review when an item becomes outdated; each location needs separate count.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Display expected quantity, stale-change signal, and reviewer reconciliation in one queue; measure rejected counts and time to approve.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Inventory count approval is payment-independent; verify approved stock reflects all tender sales exactly once, including Bitcoin sales.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Stock counts do not resolve payment finality; manager approval and inventory ledger remain separate from wallet settlement.
claims.acceptance_test: Create an admin count for a location, assign staff, count several listed items concurrently, request review, approve one and reject another, then verify only approved quantities update.

claims.capability: Create and update specific product variants with per-variant values
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can offer valid combinations while setting distinct price, SKU, barcode, inventory, image, shipping and location values per variant.
claims.trigger: Merchant introduces another product option value or edits an existing combination.
claims.behavior: Merchant adds named options and values (up to three options and 2,048 variants); can add single variants, duplicate variants/bulk combinations, or connect options to category metafields; individual variants can be edited or bulk-edited.
preconditions: Product is created in admin or Shopify app; a new variant must have at least one new option value.
qualifiers: Adding a new option value generates combinations; manually adding/duplicating one variant does not create every possible combination; variant editor UI may differ during rollout.
recovery_edge_cases: Exact duplicate variant cannot be saved; stop-selling can be done by unpublishing to preserve history rather than deleting; variant settings may need per-variant adjustment.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview generated variant combinations and inherited fields before saving; measure duplicate variants, missing price/SKU and setup time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Variant-level identity and inventory should be shared across Bitcoin and other tender; validate each variant and its stock mapping across tenders without fiat-only product duplication.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Variant metadata does not define settlement currency; any Bitcoin price presentation must preserve merchant-selected catalog price and explicit quote basis.
claims.acceptance_test: Add size/color options and inspect generated combinations; manually add a unique variant, try an exact duplicate, edit a price and location quantity, and verify expected save/rejection outcomes.

claims.capability: Create and process an inventory transfer with shipment tracking
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can stage a transfer, inspect source/destination quantity effects, then commit stock movement and track shipments.
claims.trigger: Merchant replenishes another store or receives supplier stock.
claims.behavior: Admin creates draft transfer with optional origin/destination, products and quantities; draft is editable and uncommitted; processing moves through ready/in-progress/transferred/canceled states; shipment can carry tracking, expected arrival, barcode and cost details.
preconditions: User has admin inventory transfer access; source/destination locations exist or blank endpoint represents external party.
qualifiers: Transfer quantity at destination does not automatically activate product there; receiving/activation controls sellability; bulk transfer CSV can overwrite variant quantity already on existing transfer.
recovery_edge_cases: Draft transfer can be deleted; ready-to-ship cannot be deleted and must be canceled; canceled committed quantity returns available at origin.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview source availability, destination activation, and shipment commitments in a single review before processing; measure transfer cancellation and unstocked-at-destination errors.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Stock movement is tender-independent; preserve location reconciliation and use Bitcoin only as a separate settlement rail for sales, without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A transfer is an inventory movement, not a payment; no Bitcoin settlement behavior should be inferred from it.
claims.acceptance_test: Create draft transfer between locations, inspect quantity effect without commitment, process it and add shipment details; verify transfer status and destination product activation state.

qualifiers: Receipt is on the transfer, not directly on the purchase order; individual shipments can be received separately; scanner or manual quantities supported.

claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Supplier purchase orders capture commercial terms and inventory receipt, not settlement; Bitcoin supplier payment accounting is not established by this guide.
claims.acceptance_test: Mark a PO ordered, receive linked transfer with accepted/rejected/canceled partial quantities, and verify only accepted goods are available at destination and status remains in progress for outstanding units.

claims.capability: Cashier can add a catalog item by keyword, UPC/SKU search or by scanning its GTIN when compatible scanning hardware/camera is available.

claims.qualifiers: US; documented primarily in Square Retail POS guide; Dashboard Virtual Terminal has a separate scan path.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If scan accessory/camera is unsupported or GTIN is not associated, use keyword/UPC/SKU search; docs do not state behavior for ambiguous matches.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: OpenBMT could offer fast local item lookup with scanner and resilient manual search while preserving merchant-controlled item records.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cart lookup does not require Bitcoin settlement; same cashier workflow should serve cash, card and Bitcoin tenders.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Offline/local search helps during connectivity loss but catalog synchronization conflicts may create stale prices or tax rules.
claims.acceptance_test: Given a GTIN linked to an item and a supported scanner, scanning adds that item; keyword, UPC and SKU searches resolve the same item.

claims.capability: Toast devices detect certain connectivity disruptions, present an offline banner after 40 seconds, and switch online after connectivity returns.
claims.merchant_outcome: Help staff understand connectivity state and resume connected operations after recovery.
claims.actor: Toast POS device and restaurant operator
claims.trigger: Loss and restoration of local network, internet, or Toast cloud connection
claims.behavior: Affected devices enter offline mode after detected disruption; an offline banner appears after 40 seconds with cause, available actions and resolution guidance. Once a connection is restored, the platform automatically returns the device online.
claims.preconditions: Toast POS device and the relevant offline support behavior; one device may be offline while other devices remain online.
claims.qualifiers: Offline experience varies by disruption type, synchronization method, and number of devices affected.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A lone device offline while others on local network remain online points to a device-specific issue. Router restart while using offline mode can prevent backup printing and is recommended as a last step.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide clearer per-device connectivity and recovery status; measure time to diagnose and restore.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Connectivity diagnosis benefits operations regardless of settlement model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A Bitcoin layer would not eliminate ISP, local network, or POS service dependencies.
claims.acceptance_test: Simulate device-only, LAN, ISP and cloud disruption; confirm banner timing, affected-device scope, printer behavior and automatic reconnection.

claims.capability: Offline order sharing depends on the configured synchronization method; local sync uses a local hub to distribute orders across devices.
claims.merchant_outcome: Keep supported devices coordinated during some internet or Toast service outages.
claims.actor: Toast POS devices and local hub device
claims.trigger: An order is entered while internet or Toast service is unavailable
claims.behavior: With the described legacy offline method, devices cannot share through cloud and store order data locally on each device. With offline mode using local sync, an eligible local hub distributes orders among devices on the local network even when internet or Toast service is unavailable; the hub cannot forward orders to Toast cloud until online.
claims.preconditions: Local sync available and configured with eligible local hub; local network still operating.
claims.qualifiers: Guide states Toast is migrating from the current method to local sync and plans to deprecate the old method; rollout status for a given merchant is unknown.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Online orders cannot be sent/received through Toast API during outages; all online orders sent during outage are received after restoration. Offline entry may overwhelm the kitchen when connectivity returns.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could make sync mode and queued-order backlog visible with recovery controls; measure duplicate/missed orders and kitchen surge after outage.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A direct Bitcoin or Lightning path might offer another settlement route where payment-network connectivity remains available, but the cited guide does not show that it preserves POS order sync or Toast authorization during an outage.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment settlement cannot substitute for menu, kitchen, API, and local synchronization. Any design needs explicit connectivity dependencies, duplicate prevention, authorization limits, reconciliation and outage tests.
claims.acceptance_test: Identify actual sync method and hub eligibility; simulate internet/cloud loss with LAN available, compare order propagation, then reconnect and reconcile queue without duplicate kitchen tickets.

claims.preconditions: Backup artifact is current, usable, and held by merchant.
claims.qualifiers: Key backup and sales-history backup are different; seed ownership alone does not restore application records.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Restore on clean hardware and reconcile derived addresses, UTXOs, and old issued addresses before retiring old device.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a recovery checklist and independently verifiable backup freshness/coverage indicator.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Independent key recovery can avoid a vendor account being necessary to regain authority; prove offline restore.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Merchant bears backup secrecy, physical security, and operational testing; backup exposure increases theft risk.

claims.capability: Know inbound liquidity before promising Lightning acceptance
claims.merchant_outcome: Cashier only offers Lightning when funds can actually be routed to the merchant.
claims.trigger: Lightning enabled or invoice requested

claims.preconditions: Running node with current channel and route information.
claims.qualifiers: Plan requires confirmed capacity/funding/availability gates; not a guarantee of route or payment success.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: When capacity becomes insufficient, stop offering Lightning and route customer to on-chain/cash choice without losing sale state.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose readiness as current evidence and freshness with reason unavailable, not a guaranteed capacity badge.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-operated node can control its receive availability directly; proof requires successful measured receiving under merchant-owned operational control.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Inbound capacity is finite, directional, may require capital/provider action, and can change; no free or prepaid liquidity assumption.

claims.qualifiers: BOLT invoice feature support and MPP behavior are protocol/version dependent; library selection alone is not proof.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After partial parts or node restart, recover aggregate status and avoid treating individual unresolved HTLCs as settled revenue.

claims.capability: Preserve channel state safely across backup and restore
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant does not mistake a key backup for a complete live Lightning node recovery.
claims.trigger: Backup, device migration, restore, or crash
claims.behavior: Track freshness and consistency of channel manager/monitor state; stop Lightning if required state is stale or missing; explain that seed/key possession alone may not restore current channels.
claims.preconditions: Implementation provides safe persistence and monitor synchronization.
claims.qualifiers: LDK 0.2.8 docs and BOLT protocol identify integrator state duties; LND static backup is an implementation-specific recovery comparator.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Use tested implementation recovery procedure; stale state can risk channel funds, and static channel backup may force closure rather than restore live channel state.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose backup health and recovery mode separately from key custody; gate Lightning offers on validated freshness and integrity.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant-owned keys support independent control but do not make Lightning channel state independent of peers or persistence.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Channel state requires careful consistency; recovery can require peers, force close, on-chain fees, and delayed access.
claims.acceptance_test: Inject stale/missing manager and monitor backups; verify Lightning stays disabled until safe recovery, then reconcile balances and close outcomes.

claims.preconditions: Merchant has applicable channel keys and required current state.
claims.qualifiers: Key ownership is not identical to channel-state independence; unilateral exit may not be immediate and may depend on valid state and chain access.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If provider does not cooperate, use documented unilateral close and sweep path; track timelocks and fee bump needs.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Present exit as tested procedure with time/cost estimates and identify any peer/service dependency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Self-operated channel keys can reduce provider permission dependence; validate unilateral recovery without provider approval.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No guarantee of immediate liquidity; force close requires on-chain fee and waiting periods, and state loss can be serious.
claims.acceptance_test: In isolated test channel, remove provider cooperation and recover using merchant-controlled current state; measure time, fees, and inaccessible interval.

claims.capability: Safely handle unknown required URI parameters
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant and customer do not make a payment when the wallet cannot honor a required instruction.
claims.trigger: Payment URI is parsed
claims.behavior: Treat unknown required (`req-`) parameters as unsupported and reject the entire request; ignore only optional unknown fields as permitted by the standard.
claims.preconditions: Wallet implementation conforms to URI standard and displays the resulting request for customer authorization.
claims.qualifiers: BIP 321 defines required extension handling; compatibility still varies by wallet.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If rejected, preserve sale and allow staff to issue a supported plain request only after validating the same amount and address.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Validate URI construction and expose unsupported-wallet recovery without weakening required instructions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Standards-based payment requests can interoperate while safely failing closed on required features; prove against multiple wallets.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Unknown optional data can be safely ignored per standard; unknown required parameters must not be silently discarded.
claims.acceptance_test: Create URIs with supported, unknown optional, and unknown `req-` fields; named clients must honor or reject as specified, with no payment on reject.

claims.capability: Prevent concurrent spends from selecting the same UTXO
claims.merchant_outcome: Refund and payout operations do not race, double-reserve funds, or fail after staff believe they were approved.

claims.behavior: Reserve selected UTXOs before authorization; present conflicts and release reservation only on cancel, expiry, or confirmed broadcast outcome.

claims.qualifiers: Bitcoin Core RPC offers optional UTXO locking; implementation-specific behavior must be verified.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: After crash, reconcile wallet locks and transaction mempool/chain state before retry or reuse.

claims.preconditions: Node has valid channel state and keys; chain access and fee strategy are available.

claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant keys can permit unilateral protocol exit without provider permission, provided current state and on-chain mechanisms are available.

sources.title: Payment workflows
sources.section: Cash; Credit; Guest Pay; Pre-authorizations; House accounts; Pay at a distance
sources.qualifiers: English (United States); Toast POS app; preauthorization must be enabled in settings and only a swiped card can be preauthorized; Guest Pay requires supported dual-card-reader equipment.
sources.evidence_note: Describes cash amount/change and receipt workflow; card entry, tip and authorization; split tenders below balance; Guest Pay card/tip flow; saved card tabs; house account and remote payment link paths. Card authorization failures offer cancel or another card.

sources.title: Credit card payments
sources.section: Prepaid credit cards and partial authorizations
sources.qualifiers: English (United States); prepaid card behavior differs from traditional credit cards; issuer balance constrains authorization and tip payment.
sources.evidence_note: A prepaid card with insufficient balance may partially authorize; the check remains open for another tender. Prepaid card does not cover a tip above its remaining balance.

sources.title: Transferring checks or orders to a different employee
sources.section: Transfer options; split-check behavior; permissions
sources.qualifiers: English (United States); permissions and current clock-in status apply; single transfer has different kitchen/reopen effects from bulk transfer.
sources.evidence_note: Bulk transfer of open/paid checks does not resend to kitchen; single transfer resends order, and paid/closed checks reopen. Selecting one check from a split order for single transfer transfers every check in that order; changing table is suggested for one-check reassignment.

sources.title: Refund permissions and limitations
sources.section: Permission requirements; eligible payment types; cash and card limits
sources.qualifiers: English (United States); employee requires Find Checks and Void/Refund Payments; cash refund is POS-only; card refund window is 90 days.
sources.evidence_note: Refunds supported for card, cash, and Toast gift card; not other tender, house account, or third-party gift card. Card payment may be refunded only once and only within 90 days; same-day pre-settlement reversal is a void. Cash refund from device without drawer may not appear in reports.

sources.title: Issuing a refund
sources.section: Refund types; item/service charge, whole-check and multi-payment workflows
sources.qualifiers: English (United States); original check must be found; payment type eligibility and permissions apply; Toast Web cannot print refund receipt.
sources.evidence_note: Refund choices include items, entire check, tip, tax, or custom amount. Item quantities may be fractional to two decimals and cannot exceed ordered quantity. Multi-payment refunds can be distributed across eligible tenders; omitted payment can later require custom-value refund. Removal of house/third-party/other tenders is not a refund and is not reported as one.
