decisions.title: Keep payment processor access optional and isolated
decisions.proposal: Keep card access optional and isolated from Bitcoin authority through a replaceable adapter. Do not require processor enrollment for cash or direct Bitcoin receiving.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Complete a retail checkout using the tender the merchant has enabled, with a correct sale ledger and receipt.
decisions.rationale: The standalone product includes optional third-party card processing. Its account, credential and payment lifecycle must remain separate from merchant Bitcoin keys and authority.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established direction: optional card processing, cash, merchant Bitcoin authority and independent recovery. The adapter set, eligibility, hardware and exact setup experience remain undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Review provider credential scopes and data flows; test unknown/canceled/refund outcomes; demonstrate that revoking card access leaves cash and direct Bitcoin receiving available.

decisions.title: Do not require company server permission for local checkout or recovery
decisions.proposal: Keep a usable standalone local sale and on-chain receive path without company login/approval, publisher ledger or telemetry. Any server-backed integration stays opt-in and scoped; it cannot become a hidden prerequisite for recovery.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Operate a register, receive Bitcoin, and recover keys and sale records after routine service/device failure.
decisions.rationale: Accepted purity position rejects mandatory company-server approval for recovery, telemetry, or sales-history upload; however remote-sync UX and support model remain design questions.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established constraint: no required company permission over Bitcoin funds and independent recovery. A company endpoint is not required for standalone/local cash and on-chain operation per current plan; optional service UX remains undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Demonstrate standalone cash/on-chain checkout and recovery with company endpoints unavailable; review each opt-in sync, webhook or backup service before adding.

decisions.title: Evaluate bounded owner-approved signing and UTXO protection
decisions.proposal: Preserve the current signing behavior in code while researching owner-approved bounded signing/automation for UTXO protection, fee budgets, reservations, and routine approved transactions. Define explicit transaction/value/fee/destination bounds, owner control, safe failure and recovery before implementing any change.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Protect merchant funds from uneconomic UTXOs or operational mistakes while allowing an owner to authorize routine transfers and refunds safely.
decisions.rationale: The current code exposes advisory-only UTXO guidance, but that is an implementation boundary, not a permanent rejection of protection or automation. The user said an earlier signing-control proposal was acceptable; architecture evidence and review remain necessary.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research candidate: bounded owner-approved signing control was acceptable in principle. No exact policy, automatic coin selection, consolidation, fee limits, or signing behavior change has been approved for implementation.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Produce and review a threat model, limits, authority map, state machine, failure recovery, fee/UTXO evidence and transaction-display proof; obtain approval for exact behavior before changing signing.

decisions.title: Separate recurring payment requests from standing wallet debit authority
decisions.proposal: Preserve subscription plans, cycle invoices, lifecycle notices and merchant-authorized refunds. Default recurring Bitcoin billing to a fresh customer-initiated request per cycle; do not claim a universal wallet can be auto-debited. Research any opt-in recurring spending authority separately with explicit limits, consent, revocation, destination scope and failure handling.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Bill a customer on a recurring schedule, let them pay each due cycle, manage subscription changes, and resolve missed payments or refunds.
decisions.rationale: Invoice/subscription workflows exist, but URI or invoice creation does not authorize a merchant to spend from a customer self-custody wallet. Preserving the billing job does not require assuming pull-payment capability.
decisions.user_authorization_status: merchant recurring billing job is in scope for research; customer-authorized invoice flow is a candidate. Universal automatic debit is not an established user constraint or approved mechanism.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Validate repeat invoice lifecycle and customer initiation first. Any reusable debit authority requires explicit user approval, protocol/wallet compatibility, clear consent/revocation, bounded amount/frequency, and recovery/dispute policy.

decisions.title: Treat fee and UTXO automation as a bounded protection candidate
decisions.proposal: Current UTXO fee guidance is advisory only. Research protection that can block, reserve, or request approval around uneconomic outputs and fee budgets, including bounded owner-approved transaction automation; do not infer autonomous spend authority or promise zero fees/guaranteed confirmation.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Explain what a receipt is worth now and what it may cost to spend later.
decisions.rationale: The plan describes the current code boundary as advisory with no autonomous selection/consolidation. That does not veto future automation. User accepted a signing-control proposal in principle; implementation requires exact bounds and architecture proof.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research candidate: UTXO protection and bounded owner-approved automation are acceptable for architecture study; current code remains advisory-only. Exact policy and implementation approval remain open.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Specify value and fee thresholds, privacy effects, reversibility, exception path, recovery, actual fee variance and owner controls; reviewed design before implementation.

decisions.title: Keep Shop Lightning as a core Bitcoin goal with an honest readiness path
decisions.proposal: Treat Shop Lightning as a core receiving goal, opt-in in merchant setup, with capital, inbound-liquidity, availability, persistence/recovery and independent-exit gates. On-chain-first release ordering is a proposed sequencing option; it does not defer the long-term Shop Lightning product goal. Avoid free/prepaid-liquidity and guaranteed-route claims.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Receive Bitcoin over a fast channel at the merchant’s own receiving node, and retain a safe on-chain recovery path.
decisions.rationale: The user’s product goal includes Shop Lightning; the standalone plan requires capacity/funding/availability/recovery gates. Those gates preserve honest economics without turning a proposed first-release order into product exclusion.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established goal: Shop Lightning receiving. Setup, liquidity source, exact release sequence and device coverage remain proposals to prove; no specific provider or free-liquidity assumption is approved.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Demonstrate node setup, actual funding and inbound capacity, recurring operation, backups, restore, peer/provider loss, route failures, channel exit, timelock and on-chain fees on the chosen version/device.

decisions.title: Do not promise offline Bitcoin settlement
decisions.proposal: When offline, continue only locally supported sale recording and cash tender. Show an on-chain request as awaiting observation and Lightning as unavailable when node status is stale. Keep card offline behavior provider-specific and report pending/unknown until reconciled.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Continue a cashier interaction during connectivity loss without claiming money arrived or fulfilling twice.
decisions.rationale: Bitcoin settlement requires network/node observation or later reconciliation; cached invoice/QR is not payment proof. Existing plan requires honest Bitcoin observation states and treats missing responses as unknown.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established requirement: do not misstate Bitcoin settlement when disconnected or stale. Cash fallback and tender-specific offline UX are supported job candidates; exact device behavior remains to validate.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Network/node interruption, device restart, duplicate attempts and reconnect reconciliation on target hardware; verify no false paid state or duplicate fulfillment.

decisions.title: Keep privacy local-first and multi-location optional
decisions.proposal: Keep customer identity and sales history local by default, use minimal payment-request metadata, and make multi-location synchronization or webhooks explicit opt-in with location-scoped permissions and disclosed data fields.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Complete private local checkout and reconcile each merchant location; offer an optional shared view when the owner chooses it.
decisions.rationale: Accepted purity position rules out required telemetry and sales-history upload, while the standalone plan defers universal multi-location claims. Optional service design remains undecided.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established privacy direction: no mandatory publisher telemetry or sales-history upload. Multi-location release support has not been established; optional synchronization and customer-profile design remain proposals.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Threat/data-flow review, export and webhook preview, location access matrix, retention choice, and offline behavior before enabling any shared service.

decisions.title: Treat card acceptance as replaceable and production-gated
decisions.proposal: Use the existing Square Sandbox flow as the adapter starting point, retain a provider-neutral tender interface, and do not claim production card acceptance until account, country, device, reader, outage, refund, reconciliation and privacy gates pass.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Accept cards when the merchant’s chosen provider and physical workflow are supported; preserve cash and Bitcoin choices if card service fails.
decisions.rationale: Accepted plan explicitly bounds current evidence to virtual-card Sandbox and avoids provider/country/device eligibility claims without fresh evidence.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established_constraint: card optional; production readiness unproven pending gates. A final vendor or adapter selection remains undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Fresh provider eligibility evidence and an end-to-end physical reader shift including lost responses, duplicate submissions, refunds, revocation, force-stop and relaunch.

decisions.title: Use standalone retail as the first measured validation scope
decisions.proposal: Prioritize a complete standalone retail shift and validate sale, tenders, exception handling, receipts, refunds, staff authority and closeout. Treat restaurant, online, unattended and multi-location capabilities as backlog and evidence targets, not rejected jobs or a permanent product boundary. POS integrations follow as proposed sequencing.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Serve merchants who sell at a counter today and preserve their path to restaurant, online or multi-location workflows as their needs and validation evidence justify.
decisions.rationale: The plan positions standalone retail before integrations and requires measured evidence; it does not establish a final ceiling on product scope. Existing POS later is the accepted sequence, while target workflows beyond retail remain future research.
decisions.user_authorization_status: Established sequence: standalone product before existing-POS integrations. A retail shift is the proposed first validation scenario; the exact release scope and later adapter priority remain undecided.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Complete a target retail shift, then gather merchant evidence for restaurant/online/multi-location jobs and evaluate the next workflow and integration independently.

decisions.title: Use familiar operational controls without cloning every incumbent feature
decisions.proposal: Use incumbent research to identify familiar merchant jobs and recovery cues—refunds, staff controls, split tender, local outage recovery, receipts, and closeout—then design Bitcoin-specific states and permissions around self-custody. Do not reject merchant jobs merely because one incumbent uses a custodial, hosted, or fiat mechanism.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Cashiers can finish, void, refund, hand off and close a shift with understandable status and manageable exception steps.
decisions.rationale: A vendor’s mechanism is not the merchant job. Better UX remains an empirical design question and must preserve established authority/purity goals.
decisions.user_authorization_status: research gate: merchant UX jobs are candidates for observation; exact screens/defaults are undecided. Self-custody and independent recovery remain established constraints.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Cashier observation and usability tasks with named retail workflow; measure completion time, error rate, exception recovery, receipt accuracy and training burden before design commitment.

decisions.title: Reject mandatory custodial Square Bitcoin and forced fiat conversion by default
decisions.proposal: Treat a Square-style custodial Bitcoin purchase/acceptance flow, fiat conversion, altcoin settlement or required processor account as a mechanism exception requiring separate consent. Default architecture remains direct Bitcoin receipt to merchant keys. Preserve merchant jobs of direct receive, Bitcoin refund to an owner-approved fresh destination, recurring subscription invoices and related lifecycle management; do not silently replace those jobs with gift-card/fiat/processor credit.
decisions.preserved_merchant_job: Take Bitcoin directly, retain authority and independent recovery, refund Bitcoin under merchant-approved rules, and bill subscriptions on a clear recurring schedule.
decisions.rationale: A hosted mechanism may simplify quote, conversion or reporting, but changes custody, funds permission and settlement asset. User-established boundaries favor self-custody, no required company funds permission, and Bitcoin-first product intent.
decisions.user_authorization_status: established constraint: self-custody, independent recovery, Bitcoin-first and no required company funds permission. Custodial Square Bitcoin, forced fiat conversion and altcoin substitution are not authorized as defaults; no product job is rejected.
decisions.proof_or_revisit_trigger: Only consider a specific custodial/conversion exception after explicit authorization, complete terms and authority map, asset and fees disclosure, refund/subscription path, exit plan, and direct self-custody fallback.

opportunities.title: Run a complete sale on merchant-owned Bitcoin and other tenders
opportunities.merchant_job: Sell an itemized basket, take Bitcoin/cash/optional card, issue a correct receipt, handle exceptions, and reconcile a shift; later support additional retail, restaurant, and online workflows when validated.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Adds a payment method whose on-chain receipt can be verified independently of the card processor; merchant can retain the sale ledger and key authority locally.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin does not supply a basket, tax/modifier engine, inventory, staff workflow, physical receipts, or day-close accounting. The first measured retail workflow is proposed validation sequencing; restaurant and online needs remain backlog rather than rejected product jobs.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local canonical sale journal with immutable basket and independent tender attempts; integrate on-chain and cash first, with optional replaceable card adapter and separately gated Shop Lightning receiving. Extend the same sale contract to validated restaurant and online workflows.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Local-first operation reduces backend dependence but makes durable storage, backup, reconciliation and recovery the product’s responsibility. A completed retail validation scenario does not establish restaurant or online coverage.
opportunities.validation_needed: Complete observed retail shifts on named devices; measure setup, checkout time, partial/late/excess recovery, receipt correctness, inventory/refund accuracy, day close, and support burden.

opportunities.title: Accept on-chain Bitcoin under merchant key authority
opportunities.merchant_job: Receive payment directly to merchant-controlled keys, recover independently, and keep checkout staff from gaining spend authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Supports direct receiving to merchant-controlled keys and independent recovery without required company permission over funds; checkout staff can use public-only watch access while owner-approved bounded spend automation remains a design candidate.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Self-custody does not remove key loss, device security, backup testing, privacy leakage, or staff training risks; a seed alone does not restore the merchant application ledger. Owner-approved automated spending requires explicit authority bounds and architecture proof.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Merchant hot wallet or independently created cold wallet, public-only pairing, independently verified receive address, durable issued-address mapping and merchant-held recovery artifacts. Evaluate bounded, owner-authorized signing/UTXO protection without changing signing behavior before proof and review.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Authority and possible provider independence come with direct responsibility for key protection, backups, safe address derivation, and incident recovery.
opportunities.validation_needed: Clean-device restore, watch-only pairing without secret exposure, register role denial of spend/authority changes, and correct address verification on the signer’s own display.

opportunities.title: Make payment state and sale exceptions honest
opportunities.merchant_job: Know whether a request is unpaid, partial, overpaid, late, unconfirmed, confirmed, conflicted, reorganized, expired, refunded, or unresolved before fulfillment.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: On-chain transaction and confirmation evidence can be independently checked and tied to a specific request; the merchant need not treat processor messages as the source of Bitcoin truth.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A transaction can be late, replaceable, unconfirmed, reorganized, partial, or sent after cancellation. One confirmation is not a universal fulfillment policy and an address does not expire on-chain.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Durable request-to-sale mapping and observation journal with freshness/depth, immutable transaction references, explicit exception states, idempotent reconciliation, and separate fulfillment permission.
opportunities.tradeoffs: More accurate distinctions add cashier exception work and may delay fulfillment; simplistic instant-paid indicators increase loss or duplicate-fulfillment risk.
opportunities.validation_needed: Regtest unseen/unconfirmed/confirmed/conflicting/reorged, partial/excess/duplicate, expired/late, crash/restart and restored-ledger cases; merchant selects confirmation and fulfillment policy.

opportunities.title: Control receiving and spending cost decisions
opportunities.merchant_job: Understand incoming-output future spend economics and approve outbound fee, destination, and input use with protection against avoidable UTXO loss.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Direct merchant control can make fee timing, UTXO selection and spend authorization visible rather than hiding them inside a processor payout schedule.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin cannot guarantee low fees or rapid confirmation. Tiny outputs can cost more to spend than their value; fee ceilings may delay transactions. Any automated spend behavior must be bounded and owner-approved; fresh addresses do not establish recipient identity.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Read-only satoshi/UTXO cost advisory plus a research candidate for bounded UTXO protection and fee-aware owner-approved signing, with explicit transaction preview, durable input reservation and limits. Preserve current signing behavior until architecture proof and review pass.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Advisory-only status is the current code boundary, not a permanent product limit. Automation can protect against uneconomic outputs but adds authority, race, recovery and fee-estimation risks; unbounded spending would violate the intended authority model.
opportunities.validation_needed: Define amount/fee/UTXO bounds, failure behavior, rollback and owner controls; test fee changes, dust-sized receipts, reservation races, invalid/wrong-network refund destinations, actual fee versus approved bounds, recovery and signer display. No hard maximum-loss guarantee.

opportunities.title: Offer Lightning as a separately gated receiving mode
opportunities.merchant_job: Offer Shop Lightning as a core Bitcoin receiving goal when the merchant-controlled node is funded, operational, backed up and has usable inbound liquidity.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Can support rapid wallet-to-wallet receiving without on-chain confirmation for each retail sale and can be operated under merchant node authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: It does not provide guaranteed routes, free or prepaid inbound capacity, zero downtime, instant exit, or channel-state independence from current persistent state and counterparties.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Merchant-operated Shop Lightning receiving as a core goal, with honest opt-in/setup and readiness gates for confirmed funding, usable inbound capacity, node availability, backup freshness, MPP support and independent exit. Select on-chain-first launch ordering only as a proposed release sequence; persist ChannelManager/Monitor state safely and document close/sweep path.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Faster checkout requires channel capital, inbound liquidity, connectivity, careful backups and recovery operations; force-close can incur on-chain fees and time locks. A separate initial on-chain-first release is a proposed sequencing choice, not an exclusion of Shop Lightning.
opportunities.validation_needed: Named LDK/node version and wallets; funding confirmation, directionality, liquidity acquisition cost, routing fees/failures, MPP, outage, stale backup, peer loss, reorg and unilateral exit trials.

opportunities.title: Keep payment privacy and checkout service local by default
opportunities.merchant_job: Take payment and retain sale history without mandatory company-server approval, sales-history upload, customer identity collection, or exposure of needless metadata.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: A direct wallet payment can avoid sending full payment credentials and sale records to a payment processor; merchant can use one-time addresses and local mapping.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Public blockchain activity remains observable and can be linked; address rotation is not anonymity. Local-only operation does not itself solve secure backup, device compromise, or optional service disclosure.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local journal, minimal opaque payment-request references, fresh addresses, privacy-reviewed exports, opt-in scoped webhooks only, and no required publisher ledger or telemetry.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Reducing central data collection can limit remote support, consolidated analytics and automatic multi-site views; opting into integrations creates additional disclosed data paths.
opportunities.validation_needed: Inspect URI/QR/NFC payloads, receipts, logs, exports, webhook payload/signature/retry behavior, retention and permission boundaries; test operation with no company endpoint.

opportunities.title: Continue cashier work through outages without inventing settlement
opportunities.merchant_job: Keep a sale and permitted cash/card workflows usable when network, processor, or Lightning is unavailable, then reconcile uncertain tenders safely.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Cash/on-chain choices may remain available independently of a card provider, and merchant-operated infrastructure can avoid a mandatory company server for local checkout.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin cannot be settled by a disconnected cashier or node; an offline QR/address display is only a request, not proof of received payment. Card offline authorization is provider-specific and may carry delayed decline risk.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local sale journal and cash fallback; mark card response unknown until reconciliation; disable Lightning when node status is stale; show on-chain request only as unpaid until a trusted observer catches up.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Availability differs by tender; safe status can be less convenient than an optimistic paid marker and reconciliation may require staff attention after reconnect.
opportunities.validation_needed: App kill, power/network loss, card timeout, node disconnection, remote sync conflicts, repeated attempts and post-outage reconciliation on target devices without duplicate charge or fulfillment.

opportunities.title: Reconcile refunds, receipts and day close across tender rails
opportunities.merchant_job: Tell the customer what was sold, what was received, what is owed/refunded, and reconcile exact tender totals at shift close.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: On-chain receipts and transactions provide independently reconcilable satoshi amounts and timestamps; direct merchant refunds can avoid asking an original processor to authorize Bitcoin funds.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A Bitcoin refund is a new spend with fee, destination, confirmation and authorization risks; a receipt or invoice does not prove settlement. Bitcoin does not determine tax treatment, card refund eligibility, inventory or accounting.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Canonical sale/tender/refund ledger; record refund requested/owed/paid separately, require a fresh destination and owner approval for on-chain payout, and export exact amounts with privacy disclosure.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Explicit tender-level reconciliation is more accurate but entails staff handling for exceptions and careful non-duplicative refund processing.
opportunities.validation_needed: Multi-tender partial refunds, canceled/late/excess payment, crash/retry, destination replacement, actual transaction match, receipts and day-close totals across Bitcoin/cash/card.

opportunities.title: Keep card processing optional and replaceable
opportunities.merchant_job: Accept cards when a merchant-approved provider/device is available without making that provider authoritative for Bitcoin keys or sale truth.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Merchant-controlled Bitcoin acceptance can remain available if card integration or account access changes, and card access can be isolated from Bitcoin signing authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin does not grant card-network acceptance, production eligibility, reader support, country/account eligibility, chargeback handling, or card offline approval.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Tender adapter boundary with durable card attempt IDs and unknown-response reconciliation; provider tokens and processor permissions isolated from Bitcoin wallet authority; cash/on-chain remain standalone.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Provider independence requires maintaining adapter behavior and target-device certification; additional adapters increase operations and support scope.
opportunities.validation_needed: Supported production account/country/device/physical reader evidence, lost response/duplicate/cancel/refund recovery, provider outage independence, privacy review and key isolation.

opportunities.title: Support recurring merchant billing without assuming universal wallet auto-debit
opportunities.merchant_job: Set up recurring subscriptions, present each cycle’s amount and due status, and follow up on missing payments.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: A merchant can issue a new on-chain or Lightning request for each billing cycle and reconcile direct settlement per cycle.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A payment request is not standing authority to debit a customer’s self-custody wallet. The protocol does not guarantee arbitrary recurring pull payments, customer approval, funds availability, or successful delivery.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Recurring schedule emits a distinct amount/network-scoped payment request per cycle with lifecycle notices and cancellation; customer initiates each payment. Treat any separately authorized spending arrangement as a distinct mechanism requiring explicit scope and revocation.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Customer-initiated invoices preserve explicit per-cycle wallet control but may add renewal friction and missed-payment follow-up; standing authorization could reduce friction while adding authority, revocation and dispute risks.
opportunities.validation_needed: Test recurring invoice generation, amount changes, cancel/pause/resume, late/partial/duplicate payments, failed notices, invoice expiry, reconciliation, and customer cancellation; separately review any proposed reusable spending authority.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both let an operator change the quantity of an item before completing payment.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify describes quantity controls in the cart row. Square permits preselection or editing during item configuration and says relevant quantity fields lock after saving the cart; preserve that workflow limit.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both remove an unpaid item from the active cart.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify documents selected-multiple and clear-all removal as well as one line; Square documents line removal and clear cart with confirmation. Do not assume the same undo behavior.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each exposes a customer gratuity choice or merchant-configured tip collection at checkout/POS.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify claim is eligible POS card checkout; Square documents configurable prompt timing and presets/custom/no-tip; Toast includes default, approval threshold, signature flow; BTCPay describes configurable POS tip feature/percentage presets. Keep supported modes, tender eligibility, calculation basis, settlement timing, and whether UI is merchant- or buyer-facing as claim-level qualifiers. Do not alias Square's 36-hour tip settlement with tip collection.

normalization_relationships.rationale: All support a cash tender at an in-person checkout and a recorded payment outcome.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify and Toast calculate change due when amount tendered exceeds balance. Square claim covers cash/check/other recorded tenders and explicitly says Square does not process or transfer the money; it does not currently claim the same change calculation. Keep noncash tender and change behavior separate in detailed acceptance criteria.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both describe finishing one sale using more than one tender method until the sale is fully paid.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square imposes a five-minute completion window and has a connected Terminal card restriction; Shopify's eligible POS device/method combinations are separate. Toast partial card acceptance below is deliberately excluded because its claims emphasize an open/partially paid check rather than a completed split.

normalization_relationships.rationale: These claims expose restaurant check allocation into separate guest amounts using seats, items, portions, or equal shares.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square item/portion splitting needs Restaurants Plus/Premium with New order and pay; seat splitting requires seat tracking and has limitations on fractional items, modifiers, and recombination. Toast claim includes item/equal/seat options but source-specific workflow and requirements remain intact. Square C016 is a broad summary overlapping C047-C049; keep as a vendor claim if needed but do not count it as another distinct behavior in normalized capability totals.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both let staff move an item from one check to another.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square also documents course moves and full-check/table merge in the same broader claim; Toast C033 specifically describes moving an item. Avoid treating check merge or payment transfer as the same operation.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each supports refunding an eligible order by selected item/quantity or a specified amount, including a full refund.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square's claim is specifically linked card refunds and disallows cancellation after submission; Toast also includes charges, tax, tip, full check and multi-tender refund distribution; Shopify describes POS order returns and eligible order conditions. Preserve tender-specific limits and refund destination.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both document refunding tip value as part of refund handling; Shopify makes a separate-tip refund explicit and Toast includes tips in its broad refund scope.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Toast's claim does not assert that tip can always be refunded separately from merchandise, only that tip is a supported refund component. Keep Shopify's independent tip refund capability distinct from Toast's inclusive scope until Toast evidence establishes separate handling.

normalization_relationships.rationale: These support presenting, configuring, or delivering proof of payment through print, email, SMS, app, or an automatic/default route.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: These claims document receipt-channel choice after checkout. Shopify includes Shop app and no receipt; Square offers printed/text/email according to receipt screen; Toast digital mode offers text/email or print for in-store order. Device, consent and payment-state conditions stay attached.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Square exposes reprint of paper receipt or resend of digital receipt from transaction history.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: This is a Square-only capability in current corpus, distinct from choosing receipt destination at checkout; gift and declined-payment receipts have separate paths.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both configure receipt behavior to suppress or override per-transaction customer channel choice.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square skip mode sends automatically to opted-in customers and is device-local; Toast supports device receipt mode overrides and transaction toggles. Do not assume identical consent/default behavior.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents merchant configuration of a sellable catalog entry or its selectable form: product/variant, item variation, menu item, or POS item.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify and Square model variants with option values and per-variant details; Toast describes a hierarchical restaurant menu; BTCPay POS item documentation gives title/price/description/image but not variants. Do not infer common SKU, modifier, price, or inventory semantics.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both let a merchant represent selectable product variants/options and retain values on the resulting variant records.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify supports named options and variant-level values, bulk combinations and category metafield links; Square applies reusable option sets to generate fixed variations. Their limits and import/price workflows differ. Toast modifiers are add-ons/choices, not equivalent stock-bearing variants.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both document bulk ingestion/update of catalog records from structured files rather than editing each item individually.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify uses product CSV with variants and separate multi-location inventory CSV; Square uses a mapped item-library import with row errors. Cancellation, rollback and supported columns differ.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both allow export of product/catalog data to a structured file for offline review or migration.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify export covers products/variants and has distinct inventory exports; Square can export a filtered item library. Do not assume equivalent columns or round-trip fidelity.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents an operator changing recorded item stock quantity or availability through an adjustment/quick-edit surface.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify Quick counts has POS and admin paths; Square requires tracked stock and a reason; Toast distinguishes In Stock, Out of Stock and remaining Quantity and has Web/POS manager surfaces. Approval, audit history, location scope and decrement behavior differ.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents counting physical on-hand inventory and using the count to reconcile recorded stock.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify documents scheduled, staff-attributed counts with manager review; Square separates cycle counts (uncounted items unchanged) from full counts. Square submission/approval and Shopify update timing differ.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both document creation of a stock transfer between locations with products/quantities and a transfer record.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify supports draft and shipment lifecycle details; Square documents source/destination, tracking and draft/create/export. Do not infer identical reservation or stock-decrement timing.

normalization_relationships.rationale: The claim documents the origin location preparing/scanning quantities and sending an admin-created transfer shipment.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: No Square claim in the reviewed bundle documents the same send/fulfill step at this granularity; keep this as a one-vendor normalized behavior until evidence supports an alias.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both let destination staff record receipt of transferred goods, including quantity reconciliation and full or partial acceptance.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify supports accepting all or reviewing/counting line items and accept/reject behavior; Square documents full/partial receipt and may permit instant transfer. Exception handling and inventory posting timing differ.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both document creating a customer profile in connection with merchant activity or through a customer-management workflow.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify POS creation collects at least one identity field and separately records marketing consent; Square also supports import, matching and failed-row recovery. Creation does not imply cart attachment, consent, loyalty enrollment or the same required fields.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents configuring or assigning a staff/user access profile that governs some merchant or POS actions.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify POS Pro roles gate actions and can require manager approval; Square uses configurable permission sets; Toast groups permissions into jobs; BTCPay documents role names/invitation or API assignment but not a full action matrix. Treat BTCPay role names as labels, not equivalent permissions.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both document creating a retail location record in the merchant account.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify describes default fulfillment availability and zero stock for new products at the location; Square claim describes entering profile/contact details. Neither should be conflated with BTCPay's additional payment stores or Toast hierarchy entities.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both describe choosing/switching the location context used by a POS device and its scoped activity.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify associates POS device location with tax context and Pro subscription; Square switches location-specific catalog/report/device context. Access and subscription rules are product-specific.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents ending/closing a cash handling interval and comparing or recording actual cash against expected activity.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify sessions hold opening float, cash movement and final count; Square can end a drawer with an actual count; Toast has explicit open/paused/closed states and blind/full expected-balance permissions. Session boundaries and variance calculations differ.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents establishing or configuring a cash drawer/register with a starting cash float for later reconciliation.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify sets starting float at register session; Square starts a session from POS and requires the Cash Management add-on; Toast configures default starting balance and physical drawer/device cash mode. Toast's cited claim is configuration, not proof of the same session-start UI.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each provides auditable entry of cash moving into or out of an active drawer outside an ordinary sale payment.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Square exposes generic Pay In/Pay Out with description; Toast separates Cash In, Cash Collected, payout, tip out and cash drop, with different limits/reasons and audit records.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each exposes cash activity or discrepancy information to support drawer/deposit reconciliation.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify reports register-session discrepancies and cash payments; Toast drawer screens expose balances/activity while deposit reports diagnose expected versus actual deposits. These are related reports, not the same metric or closeout workflow.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each provides an export/print/email path for operational report data or configurable export fields.
normalization_relationships.variant_cautions: Shopify exports/remote-closes register sessions; Toast configures export datasets and columns; Square exports or emails eligible reports with report-specific restrictions. This is an interaction-level alias only; data coverage and file schemas are not equivalent.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Each documents an operator choice to accept supported card tenders while the POS lacks its normal network connection, subject to product-specific limits and later processing. The shared normalized behavior is the merchant's ability to enable or stop card acceptance during an outage.
variant_cautions: Shopify describes supported credit/debit cards and configured limits.
Toast queues offline cards for later authorization and lets the merchant stop offline acceptance.
Square's control selects cash-plus-card or cash-only; tender restrictions and hardware-specific upload deadlines are separate claims.
None of these claims means card acceptance is guaranteed to succeed after reconnection.

normalization_relationships.rationale: Both Shopify claims describe a customer-facing display route for opening the merchant's published privacy policy during checkout.
variant_cautions: One claim covers the checkout/customer display presentation and the other the operational setting/configuration; policy publication and device/app support are preconditions.
Showing a policy is not itself evidence of legal compliance, privacy controls, or fulfillment of data requests.

normalization_relationships.rationale: The Bitcoin-native requirement and BTCPay watch-only wallet behavior both specify observing/receiving without retaining spend authority on the checkout/server side. The requirement describes desired product behavior; BTCPay documents one concrete wallet setup that erases the generated private key from the server.
variant_cautions: BTCPay setup still requires the merchant to retain a recovery seed or external signer and test recovery.
An imported xpub/public derivation data can reveal wallet privacy information.
Do not merge with BTO-C008 hot-wallet behavior, where the server holds a spend key, or claim company recovery authority from a watch-only setup.
Shopify describes automatic processing of stored offline payments and syncing orders.
Toast describes queued authorization, statuses, declines, and reopening backgrounded checks.
Square has a hardware-specific upload deadline and pending/completed/declined behavior.
Do not normalize this family into one generic promise that offline cards will reconcile successfully.
Toast operations documents a 40-second offline banner in its reviewed guide; the service claim names local network, internet, or Toast cloud triggers.
A device's online status does not establish tender availability, local order sharing, or service recovery.

entries.capability: Create sale with fixed amount and optional immutable item lines
entries.evidence_notes: createSale validates positive integer amount/currency and stores item snapshots; UI exposes two sample USD items and manual amount entry.
entries.limitations: No configurable product catalog, sale revisions, or full canonical basket contract.

entries.capability: Select quantity for two sample products
entries.evidence_notes: UI has two hard-coded sample items and basket review. Plan explicitly calls these a two-item sample cart.
entries.limitations: No catalog CRUD, inventory linkage, product import, modifiers, tax, discount, or tip.

entries.capability: Compute sample basket totals using integer minor units
entries.evidence_notes: Basket multiplication and aggregation use exact integer operations; ledger checks item total equals sale total.
entries.limitations: No configurable tax, discounts, tips, or immutable quote terms.

entries.capability: Convert USD amount to sats using fixed developer quote
entries.evidence_notes: Checkout code uses fixed REGTEST_USD_MINOR_PER_BTC; app calls it fixed developer test data.
entries.limitations: No live pricing source or production quote/expiry guarantee.

entries.capability: Fetch and apply live market rates in standalone checkout
entries.evidence_notes: Reviewed checkout uses fixed test quote, while rates crate supplies rate primitives/providers.
entries.workflow_scope: Standalone checkout vs shared rates engine
entries.limitations: No inspected integration of live rate source into checkout.

entries.capability: Persist immutable item name, unit amount, and quantity snapshots
entries.evidence_notes: SaleItem is snapshotted and sale creation verifies its item total.
entries.limitations: Tax, modifiers, discounts, and price-history contract are absent from this snapshot.

entries.capability: Persist Bitcoin attempt identity and quote/request reference before receiving
entries.evidence_notes: beginBitcoinAttempt records attempt ID, expected amount/sats, quote ID/time, and counter index before receiver invocation.
entries.limitations: App is marked Regtest only; no mainnet or merchant shift validation.

entries.capability: Track partial, confirmed, reorged, late, and overpaid evidence
entries.evidence_notes: Ledger retains Bitcoin evidence and derives payment state; UI flags review/late conditions.
entries.limitations: No mainnet validation; not equivalent to a production canonical commerce lifecycle.

entries.capability: Persist stable provider id before invoking card SDK
entries.evidence_notes: Checkout ledger supports stable card provider identifiers; optional Square bridge is isolated in debug Sandbox module.
entries.limitations: Production eligibility, physical reader, country/account/device support unproven.

entries.capability: Represent card pending, approved, completed, canceled, failed and unknown outcomes
entries.evidence_notes: Card states and evidence are modeled; scoped Sandbox reconciliation code is present.
entries.limitations: Does not establish production adapter reliability or production reconciliation.

entries.capability: Record manually acknowledged USD cash amount applied
entries.evidence_notes: CashPayment stores applied/tendered/change values; UI asks cashier to confirm physical receipt.
entries.limitations: USD cash only; manual operator acknowledgment, no drawer verification.

entries.capability: Preview and record change due for cash tender
entries.evidence_notes: UI computes remaining amount and change; ledger validates cash tender and persists values.
entries.limitations: No drawer integration, cash count, or non-USD cash handling.

entries.capability: Durably persist cash tender as part of local sale state
entries.evidence_notes: Cash mutation shares atomic local ledger writes and restart state; plan cites cash/restart checks.
entries.limitations: No opening float, cash-in/out, shift accounting, or cash refund support.

entries.capability: Combine recorded cash with Bitcoin/card attempt amounts
entries.evidence_notes: Sale tracks remaining balance across tenders and UI offers cash/card actions for an unpaid remainder.
entries.limitations: Complex partial/unknown/refund and canonical sale reconciliation remain incomplete.

entries.capability: Initialize local event epoch and snapshot current sales
entries.evidence_notes: initializeEvents commits epoch and current sale versions; local event data is internal checkout ledger.
entries.limitations: Not a versioned merchant event API or owner Requests API.

entries.capability: Read local event pages with cursor, floor, and resync indication
entries.evidence_notes: readEvents handles epoch mismatch/expired cursor with resyncRequired; benchmark notes bounded snapshot/replay.
entries.limitations: Bounded journal is not webhook delivery or external merchant integration contract.

entries.capability: Write ledger state atomically and detect uncertain outcomes
entries.evidence_notes: Nio storage writes temp file, forces contents, atomic-renames, then forces parent; uncertain outcome poisons/reloads state.
entries.workflow_scope: JVM/desktop storage implementation with Android adapter expected
entries.limitations: Does not establish Android power-loss behavior or full device recovery.

entries.capability: Reload locally persisted sale state after restart
entries.evidence_notes: Ledger decodes durable local state; plan says Android restart/history checks passed.
entries.limitations: No Box/backup restore, device-loss recovery, or full physical merchant workflow.

entries.capability: Search sale IDs and immutable item names
entries.evidence_notes: searchSales filters query against sale ID/item names, sorted by time; native UI exposes Sales.
entries.limitations: No customer/order-reference search or broad audit attribution.

entries.capability: Filter history by Bitcoin, card, or cash tender presence
entries.evidence_notes: HistoryTender includes all three; matching reports recorded attempts/payment, not income.
entries.limitations: Presence is not final settlement or revenue report.

entries.capability: Filter paid, unpaid, or owner-review sales
entries.evidence_notes: Status filter prioritizes requiresReview, then paid/unpaid.
entries.limitations: No advanced exception and fulfillment lifecycle reporting.

entries.capability: Filter sale history by inclusive/exclusive timestamps
entries.evidence_notes: History query supports fromInclusive/untilExclusive.
entries.limitations: No timezone/day-close report in this screen.

entries.capability: Create privacy-limited receipt projection from sale record
entries.evidence_notes: Projection contains item/tender/refund and payment status facts; strips controls from names.
entries.limitations: Projection/test text only; not proof of issued receipt.

entries.capability: Format stable plain text receipt for display/test
entries.evidence_notes: receiptText formats supported USD/SAT amounts using integer units; app renders receipt-like screen.
entries.limitations: No physical printing, email, or network delivery.

entries.capability: Record refund request against original payment attempt
entries.evidence_notes: App explicitly states recording request does not send Bitcoin or issue Square refund; ledger records request state.
entries.limitations: No customer claim-link/API flow, settlement, or provider refund invocation.

entries.capability: Track externally paid refund evidence separately from request
entries.evidence_notes: RefundEvidence and refund state track paid minor/sats, pending, and actual paid values.
entries.limitations: External owner evidence input is not an automatic payout.

entries.capability: Create and authorize on-chain returns in legacy owner/counter flow
entries.evidence_notes: Existing request/return and owner-counter flows include refund engine behavior with scoped E2E record.
entries.limitations: Not integrated into standalone checkout claim-link or refund payout UI.

entries.capability: Issue and reconcile a cash refund from standalone sale
entries.evidence_notes: Standalone plan explicitly leaves cash refund support outside current cash implementation.
entries.limitations: No cash return operation evidenced in checkout ledger.

entries.capability: Store and query owner payment requests and associated facts
entries.evidence_notes: Shared Requests crate provides ledger, model/list and returns modules.
entries.limitations: Not the standalone checkout data model or a documented merchant API contract.

entries.capability: Maintain counter-side payment/request records
entries.evidence_notes: Counter node owns legacy request/payment records and has scoped counter E2E evidence.
entries.limitations: Does not establish standalone native checkout integration.

entries.capability: Reserve or decrement inventory once per sale
entries.evidence_notes: Reviewed native sale schema has no stock fields; plan lists inventory-once as remaining work.
entries.limitations: No inventory ledger or idempotent stock workflow demonstrated.

entries.capability: Create/edit reusable products and catalog
entries.evidence_notes: UI labels sample catalog and says no provider catalog/inventory connected; plan identifies configurable catalog as backlog.
entries.limitations: Only sample products inspected; no CRUD workflow.

entries.capability: Configure or calculate sales tax
entries.evidence_notes: Native sale has amount/items without tax fields; plan leaves tax/modifier engine as remaining work.
entries.limitations: No tax workflow demonstrated.

entries.capability: Apply discounts or tips to basket total
entries.evidence_notes: Reviewed cart model tracks product, unit price and quantity only; plan lists discounts/tips as backlog.
entries.limitations: No such checkout controls demonstrated.

entries.capability: Authenticate cashier/manager/owner roles in checkout
entries.evidence_notes: Core capability type is verified metadata; plan says role screens and permission matrix remain backlog.
entries.workflow_scope: Shared metadata primitive vs standalone app
entries.limitations: Pure metadata is not authentication, staff screens, or enforcement.

entries.capability: Represent verified authorization, revocation, expiry and exact store/register scope
entries.evidence_notes: Core capabilities model pure verified metadata scoped to store/register.
entries.limitations: No authenticated transport, staff UI, or proof checkout actions enforce metadata.

entries.capability: Export guarded reconciliation CSV with satoshi amounts and timestamps
entries.evidence_notes: Books reconciliation export records exact satoshi amounts/timestamps and requires payment-disclosure acknowledgment per implementation addendum.
entries.limitations: Not complete accounting/day-close report; accountant export narrower.

entries.capability: Aggregate book totals by UTC or local day
entries.evidence_notes: Books supports UTC/local day totals, currency and tips fields.
entries.limitations: Does not constitute standalone checkout closeout screen or cash reconciliation workflow.

entries.capability: Open/close shift, count drawer, and review discrepancy
entries.evidence_notes: Plan lists opening float, cash-in/out, count, close, discrepancy review as remaining.
entries.limitations: No shift accounting/day-close workflow demonstrated.

entries.capability: Support physical receipt printer, drawer, barcode scanner or display
entries.evidence_notes: Standalone plan requires a tested capability matrix; receipt code is projection only.
entries.limitations: No physical peripheral support evidenced in inspected files.

entries.capability: Run optional Square Mobile Payments SDK virtual Sandbox flow
entries.evidence_notes: Sandbox module implements optional virtual card flow; documentation explicitly limits scope to Sandbox.
entries.limitations: Not production card acceptance, reader validation, eligibility, or privacy approval.

entries.capability: Create/observe Lightning receiving requests using configured node engines
entries.evidence_notes: Shared node/invoice types support Lightning receiving interfaces.
entries.limitations: Does not prove standalone checkout integration, funds/capacity readiness, or provider uptime.

entries.capability: Assess point-in-time confirmed funding and strict/lazy queue status
entries.evidence_notes: Node::receiving_assessment reports current confirmed-funding and strict/lazy-queue status.
entries.limitations: Assessment is not a route or capacity guarantee and not all receiver readiness.

entries.capability: Require confirmed funding before selected receiving mode
entries.evidence_notes: Funding gate exists in configured Lightning flows and specific tested paths.
entries.limitations: Does not establish every receiver mode, route, liquidity, backup freshness, or independent exit readiness.

entries.capability: Estimate UTXO spend/consolidation costs and report threshold advisories
entries.evidence_notes: Maintenance advisory estimates fees and identifies uneconomic outputs; explicitly advisory.
entries.limitations: No automatic coin selection, consolidation, transaction signing, or execution.

entries.capability: Plan transaction inputs, outputs, fees, and change for owner spending
entries.evidence_notes: Spend crate plans and validates transactions for explicit wallet requests.
entries.limitations: Not checkout receive automation or autonomous UTXO maintenance.

entries.capability: Create/restore Box-based wallet backup artifacts in legacy owner/counter workflow
entries.evidence_notes: Box packaging and legacy owner/counter backup/restore workflows have scoped evidence.
entries.limitations: Does not establish standalone checkout ledger backups, device-loss recovery, or Lightning channel-state recovery.

entries.capability: Restore standalone checkout ledger after loss or stale backup
entries.evidence_notes: Checkout ledger is local; plan says Box/device-loss recovery remains incomplete.
entries.limitations: Android backup rules and local ledger persistence do not prove tested restore drill.

entries.capability: Publish merchant webhooks from owner request or local events
entries.evidence_notes: Benchmark explicitly treats outward webhooks as optional adapter; inspected checkout events are local ledger only.
entries.workflow_scope: No webhook path identified in inspected scope
entries.limitations: No delivery/retry/signing endpoint established.

entries.capability: Operate hosted/online unattended checkout workflow
entries.evidence_notes: Plan defines standalone retail product first; online/unattended workflows are separately deferred.
entries.limitations: No public listener or hosted checkout workflow demonstrated.

entries.capability: Connect existing POS vendors to OpenBMT payment operations

Odoo README describes Odoo 18.0 Community tests with a stand-in Box; WooCommerce standalone/E2E documentation describes WordPress stand-ins. Plan defers broader POS adapters until standalone shift gates.
